full_text: Sirius becomes 422nd territory in Russia where foreigners prohibited from owning land The requirement to maintain such a list is established by the Land Code in the interest of protecting Russia’s state border MOSCOW, July 27. /TASS/. The Sirius federal territory, which has been put on the list of border areas where foreign nationals are prohibited from owning land, has become the 422nd such territory, according to TASS calculations. Russian President Vladimir Putin previously expanded the list of territories where foreign citizens and businesses, and stateless persons are prohibited from owning land. The requirement to maintain such a list is established by the Land Code in the interest of protecting Russia’s state border. Since the decree came into effect in 2011, an additional 52 territories have been included (including areas in Crimea and Sevastopol, which reunited with Russia in 2014). Meanwhile, ten territories were formally removed due to changes to or the renaming of the administrative boundaries of urban districts and municipal districts.

full_text: Putin has stripped foreigners of right to own land in Sirius The document adds the Sirius federal territory to the list of border territories where "foreign citizens, stateless persons, and foreign legal entities are prohibited from owning land plots" MOSCOW, July 27. /TASS/. Foreign citizens and stateless persons will no longer be able to purchase or even own land plots in the Sirius federal territory, according to a respective decree signed by Russian President Vladimir Putin. The document adds the Sirius federal territory to the list of border territories where "foreign citizens, stateless persons, and foreign legal entities are prohibited from owning land plots." The list was last amended in 2021, with changes affecting specific districts of the Bryansk Region. The ban on foreign ownership of land in border areas is established by the Land Code as part of legislation on state border protection, while the specific list of such territories is determined by a decree from the President of Russia.

A total of 7,894 tonnes of nuclear-tainted wastewater was discharged, containing approximately 1.3 trillion becquerels of radioactive tritium, according to local media. Hit by a magnitude-9 earthquake and an ensuing tsunami on March 11, 2011, the Fukushima Daiichi plant suffered core meltdowns that released radiation, resulting in a level-7 nuclear accident, the highest on the International Nuclear and Radiological Event Scale. Despite concerns and opposition from the international community, Japan unilaterally launched the discharge of nuclear-contaminated water from the plant into the ocean in August 2023. As of the completion of the 21st round, the cumulative volume released has reached about 165,000 tonnes. (With input from Xinhua)

The IRS issued $84 billion in tax refunds this March, about $25 billion less than they issued in March of 2022, according to BofA analysts. That led consumers to pull back in spending at department stores and on durable goods, such as appliances and furniture. That’s enough water to fill the Reflecting Pool on the National Mall about 1,600 times. The capacity of the reservoir is shrinking because of sediments flowing in from theColorado and San Juan rivers, according to the report. A major international AIDS conference got underway in Rio de Janeiro for the first time since the United States began to dramatically slash foreign aid following Donald Trump's return to the White House last year. European nations including France, Germany and the UK followed suit. "Never has donor funding fallen so far, so fast, and those most vulnerable are already paying the price," said Beatriz Grinsztejn, president of the International AIDS Society , warning that the gathering was taking place at a time of "real danger" for the battle against HIV. Once a fatal and terrifying diagnosis, scientific breakthroughs and massive funding efforts have transformed HIV into a manageable disease for millions of people. "The end of AIDS is no longer limited by science. The scientists have done their part. It's limited by inequality.
